title: An Interactive Agentic HPC Tutor for Lesson Planning, Teaching, and Assessment
problem: HPC education requires expertise in parallel programming, but teaching resources are limited and personalized instruction at scale is challenging. Traditional approaches require manual code development and external APIs.
motivation: LLM-based agents enable prompt-driven programming without traditional source code. On-premises deployment on supercomputers can provide personalized, scalable HPC education without external dependencies or subscription costs.
method: Multi-agent tutoring system with locally hosted LLM models running on leadership-class supercomputers. Each agent has a narrow role: lesson planning, concept explanation, code scaffolding, and execution. Structured prompts compose complex workflows. Per-agent history summarization prevents context overflow.
key_novelty: First prompt-driven multi-agent HPC tutor deployed on HPC systems themselves, enabling dynamic, personalized learning without external APIs or proprietary services.
contributions: Multi-agent LLM-based HPC tutoring system with specialized roles
Per-agent history summarization for context management
Scalability from single-user to classroom deployments
No external API or subscription requirements
limitations: Abstract focuses on capabilities; specific evaluation metrics on learning outcomes not provided.
primary_theme: AI-driven HPC education and skill development
